children: Mumbai: State-run Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) on Friday reported a 21.45% decline in its consolidated net profit at around 4,863 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher refinery margins were offset by losses from sale of petrol, diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

BPCL had reported a profit of 6,191.5 crore in the second quarter of the previous fiscal. Consolidated revenue from operations was up 29.7% at 1,57,818 crore against 1,21,605 crore. Its consolidated total expenses during Q2 FY27 stood at around 1.52 lakh crore against 1.66 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 and 1.15 lakh crore in Q2 FY26. "The lower profit during April-September 2026 is mainly due to suppressed marketing margin on certain petroleum products which was partially offset by higher refining margin," BPCL said in a regulatory filing. The company's marketing margins were impacted as PSU oil marketing companies have been selling petrol, diesel and LPG below market rates. As on September 30, 2026, BPCL's cumulative under recoveries on LPG stood at 17,334.40 crore (March 31, 2026: 12,318.52 crore).

title: BPCL's Net Profit Falls 21%
